pages.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: OPDA semantic-modelling website manifesto header, light-mode editorial illustration
Primary request: Create one original risograph / screenprint editorial opener showing distinct professional perspectives on the same physical British property, while keeping the place, a drawn plan and a separate report visibly different.
Scene/backdrop: off-white #F9F9F9 uncoated paper to every edge. A continuous shallow streetside working scene centred on one modest British terraced house facade and front threshold. A real adult property practitioner stands in the same scene, thoughtfully comparing the physical house with a clearly hand-drawn unlettered floor plan spread on a portable angled drawing board; a separate closed unlettered report folio rests beside the board as its own object. Two additional adult practitioners with distinct professional dress and believable human proportions observe different physical details of the same house—one looks up at the roofline, one studies the threshold—without becoming symbolic icons. All attention converges on the same real place by gaze and posture only.

Composition/framing: exact intended export 1200×403, very wide near-3:1 manifesto opener; one continuous frameless scene, asymmetrical magazine composition; complete people, heads, hands, house silhouette, plan, board and report inside quiet outer margins. The physical house is the largest anchor; the plan is obviously a paper drawing, not another building; the report is visibly separate. Not a three-box diagram, not three arches, not a triptych, not a software screen.

pages.title: From a useful question to a reviewable candidate
pages.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: OPDA semantic-modelling section header for /semantic-modelling/method/from-question-to-candidate.
Primary request: Create ONE original wide 3:1 three-panel sequential ink narrative for adults. It tells a restrained left-to-right progression from question, through comparison, to constructive challenge. Use a completely different cast and staging from any earlier image. The recurring practitioner is a slim middle-aged South Asian man with close-cropped black hair, neat moustache, mustard-gold field coat and petrol satchel. The recurring modeller is a young East Asian woman with a chin-length straight black bob, round dark glasses and coral overshirt. The reviewer is an older Black man with a close grey beard, shaved head and violet cardigan. Preserve each person's face, clothing, proportions and identity whenever they recur in this strip.
Scene/backdrop: grounded British property-inspection and modelling work on cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper to every edge. Use a more graphic side-on, shallow stage-like composition than a conventional meeting scene, with restrained architectural details and no decorative abstraction.
Panel one: in profile at a real inspection-area doorway inside a modest dwelling, the mustard-coated practitioner stands beside a clearly closed door and records a question in a small open field notebook using only broad unreadable strokes; his posture and gaze clearly connect the practical uncertainty to that closed doorway. No other person in this first moment.
Panel two: at a narrow drafting desk, that same practitioner and the coral-shirted modeller compare his field notebook and ONE separate evidence folio with purely pictorial blank marks, beside a small physical architectural study model of the doorway and adjoining wall. Keep the notebook/evidence visibly separate from the model. They are considering what description could answer the question, not operating software.
Panel three: at the same shallow work setting, the violet-cardigan reviewer challenges the proposed description on a separate draft sheet, pointing thoughtfully while presenting a clearly contrasting SECOND original source folio from his own hand. The practitioner and modeller listen. Preserve BOTH original sources as visibly separate artefacts on the table, along with the provisional description; nothing is stamped or approved. Expressions are serious, curious and provisional rather than celebratory.
Style/medium: sophisticated independent-magazine ink narrative; crisp varied-width brush-and-pen contours, some confident angular dry-brush hatching, and flat pastel opaque gouache shapes. Adult editorial illustration, observational and architectural, NOT watercolour, not caricature, not a children's cartoon, not superhero comic art.
Composition/framing: exact full 3:1 panoramic canvas, three equal shallow panels read left to right, separated by thin simple deep-purple #231F2F gutters. A low side-on viewpoint with strong lateral silhouettes; full people, full heads, important hands and complete props inside the frame; no huge blank margins. Crisp and legible at 1200x400.
